units.source_text: 信辅交朋友的原则是对方必须有才能。

en.t: Shinsuke's principle in making friends was that the other person had to possess talent.

units.source_text: 就算是品行端正的君子，如果除了品性之外没什么才能，对他来说都是没用的路人。

en.t: Even a morally upright gentleman, if he had no talent beyond his character, was to him no more than a useless passerby.

units.source_text: 不，毋宁说每次见到他们，他都自然的表现这种态度，甚至不得不揶揄这些丑角。

en.t: No, rather, whenever he met them, he naturally showed this attitude, and even could not help mocking these clowns.

units.source_text: 操行分只有六分的他，从初中到高中，从高中到大学，在几个阶段的学校生活里，他总是不由的嘲笑那种人。

en.t: With only six points for conduct, he moved from middle school to high school and from high school to university, and at each stage of school life he was always unable to keep from laughing at such people.

units.source_text: 他们之中当然有人对这种嘲笑感到愤怒。

en.t: Among them, of course, there were some who grew angry at this ridicule.

units.source_text: 不过，也有人对这种嘲笑始终保持正人君子的态度。

en.t: However, there were also some who maintained the attitude of proper gentlemen toward this ridicule from beginning to end.

units.source_text: 对于自己被称为“令人讨厌的人”，他还多多少少感觉开心。

en.t: He even felt more or less pleased at being called an unpleasant person.

units.source_text: 可是，不管怎么嘲讽对方，却得不到任何回应，他就不得不愤怒了。

en.t: But when no matter how he mocked the other person he received no response at all, he could not help becoming angry.

units.source_text: 其实，曾经有过这样一个君子——高中时候的一个文科同学，一个利文斯通的崇拜者。

en.t: In fact, there had once been such a gentleman: a humanities classmate from high school, an admirer of Livingstone.

units.source_text: 信辅在跟他住同一间校舍的时候，曾经信口开河的对他说，连拜伦读了利文斯通的传记之后，也感动的流泪满面。

en.t: When Shinsuke was living in the same school building as him, he once casually told him that even Byron, after reading Livingstone's biography, was so moved that his face was covered with tears.

units.source_text: 从那个时候开始，到现在已经过去了二十年了，那个利文斯通的崇拜者在某基督教会机关志上，还在歌颂斯文利通。

en.t: Twenty years had already passed since then, and that admirer of Livingstone was still praising Livingstone in the bulletin of a certain Christian church.

units.source_text: 不仅仅是这样，文章的开头还有这样一段话：“连恶魔诗人拜伦读了利文斯通的传记也感动的泪流满面，这让我们想到了什么呢？”

en.t: Not only that, but at the beginning of the article there was also a passage like this: Even the demonic poet Byron read Livingstone's biography and was moved to tears; what does this make us think of?
